newsitem.title: UK: Copper seen heading to $2,600 and beyond-Waterside.
newsitem.headline: Copper seen heading to $2,600 and beyond-Waterside.

text.p: LME three months copper should decline to $2,425 per tonne before resuming its uptrend to around $2,600, and then will eventually take a shot at $2,800, Waterside Futures said in its latest report.

"The more recent advance from April's low at $2,240 is calculated to end between minimum $2,594, maximum $2,618, at which point a reversal decline will begin another of the deep retracements," said the broker's Wavetrack report, which uses Elliott Wave technical analysis.
On Tuesday, LME three months copper officially settled at $2,507.
A fourth wave is expected to develop during the next week with a completion towards $2,425, said the report, released on Tuesday morning.
In the long term, the advance in prices from last year's low of $1,745 is ultimately scheduled to complete late this year or early next year at a target of around $2,852.
"This will form part of the longer term trading range (triangle) pattern that is constricting activity within a narrow band," it added.
In aluminium, last week's low at $1,572 has concluded a decline from $1,680 touched in May.
"The next advance can now begin, this time a Fibonacci 2.618 percent ratio is used to comply with ongoing targets, yielding levels for this sequence towards $1,933," it said.
"A sustained and gradual advance may take place during the next few weeks, but ultimately an explosion will occur," the report added.
